text:
anya: Quick scoreboard for Newton-11b onboarding — ran PT1 bench + GTN slice. TL;DR: int6 saves ~2.9x token cost vs fp16, int8 ~1.8x; average qual drop ~1.6% on GTN prompts, but some slices (legal longform) see 3.8% recall drop.
kevin: numbers? need cost per 1M tokens and p99 lat.
anya: Roughs: fp16 ~ $1,200 / 1M tokens; int8 ~$650 / 1M; int6 ~$420 / 1M (inc. packing/throughput). p50/p95/p99 on 1xA100: fp16 18/28/78ms, int8 14/22/90ms, int6 12/20/105ms (note p99 tail worse due to IO/KV pressure).
ravi: where did quality come from?
anya: GTN test set (multi-turn product help prompts, 12k examples) + internal evals. Delta measured as % win-rate vs prod baseline (cedar11b-int6). Newton-int6 overall -1.6% win, but legal/legal-longform -3.8% on recall metrics.
sam: any latency-sensitive product slices? search autocomplete + chat quick replies.
anya: yes — autocomplete latency budget = 50ms p95. Newton-int6 p95 ~20ms but p99 105ms — tail might violate SLAs for very bursty traffic.
kevin: so routing rules needed.
anya: suggested routing rules snippet:
```
# route rule (pseudocode)
if request.slice in ["autocomplete","quick-reply"] and request.max_tokens < 32:
    route -> cedar11b-int6
elif request.priority == "latency-sensitive":
    route -> cedar11b-int6
else:
    route -> newton11b-int6
# fallback when p99_latency(newton11b-int6) > 120ms: route 20% -> newton11b-int8 or 7b-int8
``` 
ravi: what's the canary plan? numbers for statistical power?
anya: recommend 7-day canary, 10% traffic, split: 70% newton-int6, 20% newton-int8 (fallback channel), 10% holdback to prod baseline. Need ~20k sessions per arm to detect ~1.5% quality delta with 80% power on our metric.
kevin: ops/regression controls?
anya: gating: if overall win-rate delta <= -2% OR latency p99 increase > +30ms OR user-reported regressions > 0.5% => rollback. Add slice-level alerts for legal-longform recall drop > 2%.
sam: suggested product guidance for GTN: don't switch default ML model for billing-sensitive flows until 30-day econ shows >15% token cost reduction net of quality eq.
kevin: agree. also add quantization cookbook note: int6 benefits vary with prompt length — short chats get more econ upside.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/newton11b-int6 -> 2026-03-22T03:00:00Z. :rocket:
anya: final recs: 1) run 7d canary at 10% with holdback; 2) route latency-sensitive slices to cedar11b-int6; 3) monitor slice recall for legal-longform, rollback if drop>2%; 4) measure real token econ after 30d before expanding default. I'll post the bench spreadsheet + eval artifacts here: https://redwood.gists/newton11b-econ
kevin: thanks — can you add the small script to compute per-token unit econ? i'll put it in the onboarding doc.
anya: done, snippet below:
```
def unit_cost(tokens, model_rate_per_hour, tok_per_hour):
    return (model_rate_per_hour / tok_per_hour) * tokens
# example: tokens=1_000_000, rate=12 (USD/hr), tok_per_hour=10_000_000 -> cost ~1.2k
```
ravi: ok let's kick the canary. I'll book an ops window and add alerts.
sam: +1, add a feedback channel for product QA.
anya: creating PR for routing rules now. will link.
